books.title: The One-Person Company
books.subtitle: How AI Agents Are Creating the Business of the Future
books.category: Business & Economics, Entrepreneurship, Computers, Artificial Intelligence
books.positioning: The One-Person Company sits at the intersection of AI, entrepreneurship, and organizational design. It's not a coding manual and not a hype book, it's a grounded look at how AI agents are lowering the cost of running core business functions (sales, marketing, ops, finance, support, product), and what that means for who gets to start a company and what the founder's job becomes. The book follows a fictional entrepreneur, Maya, as a throughline alongside real, sourced evidence on where agent technology actually stands today, and hands readers practical frameworks for designing, governing, and scaling their own AI-augmented business.

insideItems.title: Why This Is Different
insideItems.body: What's genuinely new about AI agents vs. old software, and why the barriers to starting a company are falling (Ch 1–3).

insideItems.title: Build Your AI Department
insideItems.body: Hands-on frameworks for standing up an AI executive assistant, sales, marketing, ops, finance, and product function (Ch 4–10).

insideItems.title: Design the Whole System
insideItems.body: The Twelve-Step Blueprint for coordinating multiple agents, plus the real economics and ROI math (Ch 11–13).

insideItems.title: Run It Safely, Look Ahead
insideItems.body: What your own job becomes, the failure modes to govern against, and a 30-day plan to actually start (Ch 14–20).

insideItems.title: Start This Month, Not Someday
insideItems.body: A concrete 30-day plan that turns everything in the book into your own working blueprint (Ch 20 / Appendix D).

forItems: Entrepreneurs and aspiring founders wanting a serious, non-hyped framework for using AI agents in a business
Freelancers and consultants ready to extend their capacity without hiring
Small-business owners deciding what to delegate to AI vs. keep human
AI-curious but non-technical readers who want frameworks, not code
Anyone wanting a structured 30-day plan to design their own AI-augmented company
notForItems: Readers looking for a coding or prompt-engineering manual
Anyone wanting a "type a sentence, get a company" hype pitch

books.title: Ai handbook for kids
books.subtitle: A clear, no-jargon guide to understanding artificial intelligence, built for curious 09-to-13-year-olds who want the real explanation, not the hype.
books.author: Shukto Press
books.category: Primary (BISAC): JNF051000, Juvenile Nonfiction › Computers › General Strong alternate: JNF053000, Juvenile Nonfiction › Science & Nature › General
books.positioning: AI Handbook for Kids is a clear, no-hype guide to what artificial intelligence actually is, how it learns, where it already shows up in daily life, and how to think about it critically instead of fearfully. It's written for readers who keep hearing adults talk about "AI" without ever getting a straight explanation. What sets it apart is that it doesn't dumb things down or lean on sci-fi tropes: real concepts like machine learning, hallucination, and bias are explained in plain language, backed by a hands-on activity and a glossary kids can actually use. In 21 pages and 17 chapters, it turns "AI is confusing" into "I can explain this to my parents.

insideItems.title: What AI Actually Is
insideItems.body: The real difference between AI and a calculator, how computers "think" in patterns instead of understanding, and how machine learning actually works.

insideItems.title: AI Already in Your Life
insideItems.body: Chatbots, self-driving cars, video game enemies, recommendation feeds, and camera filters, explained through the tech kids already use every day.

insideItems.title: Thinking Critically, Not Fearfully
insideItems.body: Busting the "robots will take over" myths, understanding why AI can be biased or wrong, and knowing when to double-check instead of trust blindly.

insideItems.title: Try It, Don't Just Read It
insideItems.body: A hands-on activity for catching a real chatbot hallucinating, a self-check quiz, a look at future AI careers, and a glossary built to actually be used.
